milestone.title: Verifier timeout hardening — per-AC MP_VERIFY_TIMEOUT_SECS cooperative-flag + killpg pattern (B-52, ER-5)

intent.outcome: After this ships, the per-AC verification timeout path in `crates/mp/src/ac_verify.rs` reliably cancels runaway verifications: the cooperative `cancelled` flag is checked at every poll, and when it flips, the child process group is killed via `killpg(pgid, SIGKILL)` so no orphan subprocess survives the timeout. M107's ER-5 reviewer finding (B-52) is closed.

problem.description: M107's external review (REVIEW-NOTES-M107.md, ER-5) flagged that the per-AC `MP_VERIFY_TIMEOUT_SECS` cancellation path may leave orphan subprocesses after timeout. M106 already added cooperative-flag checking and bounded drain-thread joins, and M107 added a global deadline with `process_group(0)` + `killpg` on the spawned child. The reviewer's follow-up (B-52, status `active` in backlog.json, no owner milestone) asks to harden the *per-AC* timeout path with the same cooperative-flag + killpg pattern, closing the gap between the global-deadline path (covered) and the per-AC path (which may rely on the child's own exit when the timeout fires, without an explicit killpg on per-AC timeout). This is the same code area M110 touches for gate caching (`ac_verify.rs::run_one`); it depends on M110 having shipped so the caching and hardening land on the same code shape.

in_scope: Harden the per-AC timeout path in `crates/mp/src/ac_verify.rs::run_one` (and `verify_milestone_in`/`verify_step_tests_in` callers) with the cooperative-flag + killpg pattern: when the per-AC `MP_VERIFY_TIMEOUT_SECS` deadline fires, flip the `cancelled` flag, then `killpg(pgid, SIGKILL)` the child's process group (pgid == child_pid since each child is spawned with `Command::process_group(0)` per M107 S3). Join drain threads on a bounded deadline (~2s, same as the global path). Pinned by an integration test that runs a verification command that sleeps longer than the per-AC timeout and asserts the child is reaped (no orphan).
Document the cancellation contract in `crates/mp/docs/verifier-cancellation.md` (extend the existing M107 note to cover the per-AC path explicitly, not just the global deadline).
out_of_scope: Changing the per-AC timeout default (300s) — that's a separate config decision; this milestone only hardens cancellation.
The gate command cache (M110 S1) — adjacent code, different concern.

acceptance_criteria.description: Per-AC timeout path applies killpg on the child's process group when the per-AC `MP_VERIFY_TIMEOUT_SECS` deadline fires (mirroring the global-deadline path M107 S3 added). The `cancelled` flag is flipped before killpg. An integration test spawns a verification command that sleeps longer than the per-AC timeout (e.g. `sleep 30` with `MP_VERIFY_TIMEOUT_SECS=1`) and asserts the child process is reaped — no orphan survives. The test also asserts the gate reports `verification timed out after Ns` (existing contract preserved).
acceptance_criteria.evidence: AC-01 (per-AC killpg hardening) verified: cargo test -p mp --test ac_verify_per_ac_timeout_killpg. Test exercises 2 cases: per_ac_timeout_killpg_kills_child_process_group (a sleep-N timeout triggers killpg; child process group is reaped, no orphan survives) and cooperative_cancel_path_also_uses_killpg. The cooperative-flag + killpg pattern in crates/mp/src/ac_verify.rs::run_one mirrors M107 S3's global-deadline path.

acceptance_criteria.description: `crates/mp/docs/verifier-cancellation.md` documents both cancellation paths (global deadline + per-AC timeout) with the cooperative-flag + killpg contract. The per-AC path is no longer implicit.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: AC-02 (per-AC path docs) verified: grep -A20 -i 'per-AC\|MP_VERIFY_TIMEOUT_SECS' crates/mp/docs/verifier-cancellation.md returns the new row in the cancellation-path table ('Per-AC timeout (MP_VERIFY_TIMEOUT_SECS) | Verifier exceeds its per-AC deadline | killpg + child.kill() + child.wait() + bounded-join drains (M117 S1) | per_ac_timeout_killpg_kills_child_process_group'). The per-AC path is no longer implicit; it's documented alongside the M107 global-deadline path.

design_decisions.choice: M117's real code prerequisite is M110 S1 (gate cache in ac_verify.rs::run_one), which is already done/verified — NOT M116. The depends_on chain (M116 → M117) is sequential-only per the user's request to keep the milestone queue linear; there is no code coupling between M116 (docs/meta-tooling) and M117 (verifier hardening). If prioritization shifts, M117 can be pulled forward immediately after M110 without breaking anything.
design_decisions.rationale: Documenting the real prerequisite lets a future groom pass re-order the queue without re-discovering the coupling. The ac_verify.rs file is touched by three milestones (M110 S1 gate cache, M117 S1 killpg, and transiently M111 S6 pre-flight which was corrected to commands/milestone.rs only). M110 and M117 are the two that genuinely own run_one; sequencing M117 after M110 (already satisfied) is what matters, not after M116.

design_decisions.choice: depends_on corrected from [116] to [110] during M111-M117 adoption prep. M116 has no code coupling with M117. M117's real code prerequisite is M110 S1 (gate cache in ac_verify.rs::run_one), which shipped before this batch. The depends_on: [116] was a queue-order placeholder, not a code dependency. Chain is now M110 → M111 → M112 → M113 → M114 → M115 → M116 → M117.
design_decisions.rationale: M117's own design_decisions section already identified this discrepancy. The milestone's header was out of sync with its own analysis. Correcting it before adoption prevents a spurious wait on M116 when M117 could execute immediately after M110/M111.

design_decisions.choice: depends_on: [116] is intentional queue ordering — it ensures M117 is adopted after M116 in the 111→…→117 sequence. depends_on is used as a sequencing constraint here, not as a code coupling signal. The code coupling is to M110 S1 (gate cache in ac_verify.rs::run_one), which already shipped before this batch. The DD added during prep that claimed otherwise was based on incorrect assumption and will be removed via M111 S4 once design-decision update/remove is available.
design_decisions.rationale: Queue ordering and code coupling are separate concerns. Using depends_on for sequencing is valid; the code prerequisite to M110 is already satisfied. The conflicting DD (index 1, added during prep) is superseded and will be cleaned up after M111 ships.

steps.action: Harden the per-AC timeout path in crates/mp/src/ac_verify.rs::run_one (and the verify_milestone_in / verify_step_tests_in callers). When the per-AC MP_VERIFY_TIMEOUT_SECS deadline fires: (1) flip the shared cancelled flag, (2) killpg(pgid, SIGKILL) the child's process group (pgid == child_pid since each child is spawned with Command::process_group(0) per M107 S3), (3) join drain threads on a bounded ~2s deadline. Mirrors the global-deadline path M107 S3 added; closes the gap where per-AC timeout relied on child self-exit.
steps.done_when: Integration test spawns a verification command that sleeps longer than the per-AC timeout (e.g. sleep 30 with MP_VERIFY_TIMEOUT_SECS=1) and asserts (a) the child is reaped — no orphan process survives, and (b) the gate reports "verification timed out after Ns" (existing contract preserved).
steps.evidence: S1 closed: cargo test -p mp --test ac_verify_per_ac_timeout_killpg (2/2 green: per_ac_timeout_killpg_kills_child_process_group, cooperative_cancel_path_also_uses_killpg). crates/mp/src/ac_verify.rs::run_one now applies cooperative-flag + killpg on per-AC timeout; mirrors M107 S3's global-deadline path. WP1 closed.
